title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck works with 'ateliers' (workshops). An atelier is a set M of figures or multistrata. It carries a partial order ≤ (inclusion), a relation ≪ (roughly 'is a closed piece or sub-stratum of'), and a disjointness relation ∥. A further datum F̃ is attached to figures, apparently a family or filter of sub-figures. On p.10 he stated compatibility axioms (At CD 2 for 'special' ateliers, At CD 2' for 'polyideal' ones). Both are phrased through ≪ and ∥, and he stressed the central role of the disjointness relation.

Paragraph 1 of p.11 proposes a programme. One should isolate an axiom characterising special or polyhedral ateliers purely in terms of the structure (M, ≤, ≪, ∥), setting aside the datum F̃. For figures of finite type F̃ is presumably determined by the rest. In general F̃ reduces to certain subfamilies, via a notion of locally finite family of strata. A sentence 'In the case of special ateliers, one has…' and an 'Axiom(s) of the 3 points' are struck out.

Paragraph 2 reports a difficulty: 'Je tombe sur un bec' (French idiom: I hit a snag). In formalising ≪ for a simplicial (more generally polyhedral) atelier, he had assumed that ≪ between simplices (in a topological or tame — 'modéré' — space, say) is just the relation of set-theoretic closed inclusion. Consequently he must accept embeddings of Δ¹ into Δ² as curved arcs. The two drawings are:
- an arc bulging from the interior of the base;
- an arc joining two vertices of the base through the interior.

This in turn forces him to accept subdivisions of Δ² into two 'triangles'. Take Δ² with vertices L, R (base) and T. Draw a curved arc from L to R inside Δ², and mark a new vertex × on the base segment. The pieces are:
- the upper triangle (L, T, R) with edges LT, TR and the arc LR;
- the lower triangle (L, ×, R) with edges L×, ×R and the arc.

Combinatorially this is a perfectly good simplicial complex (two 2-simplices glued along an edge) triangulating the disc compatibly with the boundary. But the lower 'triangle' has collinear vertices, so 'nobody would regard it as a simplicial subdivision'. He diagnoses that the rigidity of affine simplices in affine space has guided the tradition. The sentence breaks off, apparently heading towards the conclusion that one must free oneself from this rigidity. The next page instead refines the compatibility criterion, separating 'polyhedral' from 'special' ateliers and introducing a 'polyhedral' strict compatibility.

What the page serves: deciding which notion of 'simplex', 'face' and 'subdivision' is intrinsic to a tame-topological, order-theoretic foundation of polyhedral and stratified geometry. The choice is between curvilinear simplices with purely topological faces and the affine-rigid PL notion.
errors: No outright error. The informal claim that the depicted decomposition is not a simplicial subdivision is right only relative to the affine/PL convention: as an abstract simplicial complex with a topological realisation it is a valid triangulation of Δ² refining the boundary (the base edge is split at ×).
The programme of eliminating F̃ is only sketched ('etc..'); no axiom is actually stated on this page.

ideas.what: Axiomatise polyhedral/special ateliers purely through the order-theoretic structure (M, ≤, ≪, ∥), recovering the extra datum F̃ from locally finite families of strata.
ideas.modern_name: Order-theoretic / face-poset description of stratified or polyhedral spaces (cf. CW posets, cell posets, exit-path posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Björner (CW posets, 1984); poset-stratified space literature (Lurie, Higher Algebra appendix; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka)
ideas.where_published: Only the general wish for tame-topology foundations is in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6; the 'atelier' formalism is unpublished.

ideas.what: Taking ≪ between simplices to be mere set-theoretic closed inclusion forces curved embeddings of Δ¹ in Δ² and 'curvilinear' subdivisions with collinear vertices.
ideas.modern_name: Topological vs PL/affine triangulations; curvilinear (definable) simplices as in o-minimal triangulation
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimal triangulation theorem (van den Dries, 1998; earlier Łojasiewicz, Hironaka for semialgebraic/subanalytic sets)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 criticises the inadequacy of PL/affine frameworks for 'topologie modérée', but not this specific example.

ideas.what: Diagnosis that the 'rigidity of affine simplices in an affine space' has shaped the notion of simplicial subdivision, and that a tame theory must abandon it.
ideas.modern_name: Intrinsic (non-affine) notion of subdivision in tame topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in o-minimal geometry and in the theory of regular CW complexes
ideas.where_published: Spirit of Esquisse d'un programme §5; explicit remark unpublished as far as I know.

missed.claim: Programme to characterise 'polyhedral' and 'special' ateliers by axioms on (M, ≤, ≪, ∥) alone, with the auxiliary datum F̃ reconstructed from locally finite families of strata. Left as a wish, then redirected on p.12 into a distinction between 'polyhedral' and 'special' axioms.
missed.quote: Il serait sans doute intéressant de dégager un axiome pertinent des ateliers spéciaux ou polyédraux, en termes cette fois de (M, ≤, ≪, ∥) — en laissant de côté la donnée de F̃
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A purely poset-plus-disjointness axiomatisation of tame polyhedra would be a combinatorial counterpart of o-minimal structures. It is related to current interest in poset-stratified spaces, but such an axiomatisation does not seem to exist in this form.

missed.claim: His example of a curvilinear subdivision of Δ² (a curved edge joining two vertices plus a new vertex on the base) is exactly what o-minimal/definable triangulations allow. He identifies affine rigidity as the obstacle to an intrinsic notion of subdivision in a tame ('modéré') framework.
missed.quote: que personne ne regarderait comme une subdivision simpliciale ! C'est la rigidité des simplexes affines dans un espace affine qui a guidé les gens
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This makes explicit Grothendieck's link between his 1986 atelier formalism and what became o-minimal tame topology. It documents that he considered non-affine, purely topological faces as the right primitive, a nuance absent from accounts based only on the Esquisse.

deep.surprise_reason: The page belongs to the unpublished but known 'Analysis situs' atelier project. Its content is a programme sketch plus a perceptive remark on curvilinear simplices that tame topology later naturalised. It is interesting but not a hidden result.
transcription_corrections: 'J[?] lambda[?] sur un bon [-voisinage[?]-] {+voisinages[?]+}' should read 'Je tombe sur un bec', the French idiom for hitting a snag. A struck/overwritten word sits above 'bec'.
'(d'un espace topologique au modèle, disons)' likely reads '(d'un espace topologique ou modéré, disons)', i.e. a tame space.
'— via d'une notion de famille loc. finie de etc..' more likely '— i.e. d'une notion de famille loc. finie de str..' (strates). 'loc. finie' is underlined.

The second figure in the '~' pair is better described as a triangle with an arc joining the two base vertices through the interior; the first shows an arc bulging up from an interior segment of the base.
Last line: 'et il faut entièrement[?]' — possibly 'et il faut entièrement s'en libérer' (cut off at the page end).
